facts.statement: The largest known individuals of Corosaurus measured more than 4 meters in length.
facts.quote: The holotype measured about 1.65 m long, while larger specimens would have belonged to individuals measuring more than 4 m long.

facts.statement: Fossils of Corosaurus were found in Jackson Canyon, Wyoming, dating to approximately 247.4 to 245 million years ago.
facts.quote: All specimens were collected in Jackson Canyon, Natrona County, from the Chugwater Group of the Alcova Limestone Formation, dating to the late Olenekian stage of the late Early Triassic, about 247.4-245 million years ago.

facts.statement: Glenn William Storrs described additional specimens of Corosaurus in 1991.
facts.quote: Later, the referred specimens YPM 41030-41068, FMNH PR 135, FMNH PR 1368-1369, FMNH PR 242-246 and FMNH PR 1382-1383 were described by Glenn William Storrs in 1991.

facts.statement: Ermine Cowles Case named the genus Corosaurus in 1936.
facts.quote: Corosaurus was first named by Ermine Cowles Case in 1936 and the type species is Corosaurus alcovensis.

facts.statement: The species name 'alcovensis' refers to the Alcova Limestone Formation where the holotype was discovered.
facts.quote: The specific name is derived from the name of the Alcova Limestone Formation, in which the holotype was found.

facts.statement: Oskar Kuhn established the family Corosauridae for Corosaurus in 1961.
facts.quote: Corosaurus was placed in its own family, Corosauridae, which named by Oskar Kuhn, in 1961.

facts.statement: Olivier Rieppel classified Corosaurus as the sister-taxon to a group containing Cymatosaurus, Pistosaurus, and Plesiosauria.
facts.quote: After a revision of the holotype and referred material of Corosaurus, Olivier Rieppel found Corosaurus to be the sister-taxon to a clade comprising Cymatosaurus, Pistosaurus and Plesiosauria.

facts.statement: The Paleobi Database lists the parent group of Corosaurus as Eosauropterygia.
Corosaurus is an extinct genus of pistosauroid found in Wyoming, United States.
facts.quote: Corosaurus is an extinct genus of pistosauroid known from Wyoming of the United States.

facts.statement: Corosaurus lived during the late Early Triassic period, specifically the late Olenekian stage, between 247.4 and 245 million years ago.
facts.quote: dating to the late Olenekian stage of the late Early Triassic, about 247.4-245 million years ago.
